Calculate RF-EMF doses with their uncertainty for ALL samples

calculate_emf_doses_stochastic.Rd

Stochastic version of calculate_emf_doses(): calculates the doses of each row many times, each time with other parameter values and input values drawn from their distributions, and summarises the doses of all draws.

Usage

calculate_emf_doses_stochastic(
  data,
  tissue,
  n = 1000,
  params = NULL,
  distributions = NULL,
  input_distributions = NULL,
  default_value_file = NULL,
  sar_file = NULL,
  sar_sd = 0.25,
  draw_inputs = TRUE,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975),
  keep_draws = FALSE,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame. Must have the exact same columns as the provided example dataset. Columns must not be missing. Missing values will be replaced with default values.

tissue

Tissue for which to calculate dose (default: "brain" or "body")

n

Number of parameter sets (draws)

params

(experimental) Path to a parameter file in .yaml format, as for calculate_emf_doses(). Its values are the means of the distributions.

distributions

(experimental) Path to a distribution file in .yaml format, with the structure of the internal distribution file (params_distributions.yaml). Optional; if not specified, the default distributions are used.

input_distributions

(experimental) Path to an input distribution file in .yaml format, with the structure of the internal input distribution file (input_distributions.yaml). Optional; if not specified, the default input distributions are used.

default_value_file

List of default values to replace missing values (optional).

sar_file

SAR values (optional): the name of a SAR file included in the package (e.g. "goliat_average", the default; see available_sar_files()) or the path to your own .yaml file, as for calculate_emf_doses().

sar_sd

Standard deviation of the SAR values, relative to their value (default: 25%). With 0, the SAR values are not drawn.

draw_inputs

If FALSE, the inputs are not drawn.

probs

Probabilities of the quantiles of the doses (default: median and 95% interval)

keep_draws

If TRUE, also return the doses and parameters of every draw.

seed

Random seed for reproducible draws (optional), as for set.seed(). The random state of the session is restored afterwards. If NULL, the draws continue from the current random state.

Value

A data frame with one row per row of data and dose, in mJ/kg/day:

  • sample_id: ID of the row, if data has a column sample_id

  • row: row of data

  • dose: exposure source (as the columns of calculate_emf_doses()), or total_dose for their sum

  • deterministic: dose with the parameter values of the parameter file, as calculated by calculate_emf_doses()

  • mean, sd: mean and standard deviation of the doses of all draws

  • one column per quantile of the doses of all draws (e.g. q2.5, q50, q97.5)

With keep_draws = TRUE, a list with this data frame (summary), the doses of every draw (doses, an array row x draw x exposure source), the drawn parameters and SAR values (params, a matrix draw x parameter) and the drawn inputs (inputs, a list of matrices row x draw, one per input).

Details

The parameter sets are drawn with simulate_params(): parameters with a distribution (see load_distributions()) and the SAR values vary around their value in the parameter and SAR files; all other parameters keep their values. Every row is calculated with the same parameter sets.

The inputs are drawn with simulate_inputs(): inputs with a distribution (see load_input_distributions()) vary around their value in data, or around their default value if missing; all other inputs keep their values.

The model takes the travel time from the time at home. If the travel time of a draw is longer than the drawn time at home, it is capped at the time at home, with a warning.

The doses of a row do not depend on the other rows. Give a seed (or use set.seed() before) for reproducible results: the same seed and arguments give the same draws.

See also

calculate_emf_doses(), simulate_params()
